title: setDispatcherHook does not settle pending mint-debt from the old dispatcher before swapping
regression-risk: pre-existing (noted in CS-12 prior audit, not separately tracked)
description:
`setDispatcherHook` replaces the configured dispatcher without first calling `_syncBudget()` or `_updatePool()`. If the OLD dispatcher has any accrued mint-debt that has not yet been pulled in, that mint-debt is effectively stranded — the new dispatcher will not know to pull from the old one, and there is no code path that pulls from the old address after the pointer changes. The NEW dispatcher's state (if any pending accrual exists) is also not reconciled.

Additionally, there is no zero-address check — owner can set the hook to `address(0)`, which `_syncBudget` handles correctly (early return), but which silently disables all future pull-based funding. This is a centralization concern (CS-12 from prior audit), but the absence of a pre-swap settlement is a separate code-level ordering bug.
impact: Owner-triggered; if owner performs a dispatcher swap without first manually calling `pullAndRefresh`, all pending mint-debt at the old dispatcher is stranded. Medium-low severity — recoverable only by re-pointing the dispatcher back to the old address to pull, or by the old dispatcher exposing a recovery path (out of scope here).
proof: Sequence: (1) old dispatcher has accumulated 1000 phUSD of mint-debt. (2) Owner calls `setDispatcherHook(newHook)`. (3) `dispatcherHook` now points to newHook. (4) A user calls any user action — `_syncBudget` calls `newHook.pull()`, which returns 0 (newHook hasn't accrued anything yet). (5) The 1000 phUSD at the old dispatcher is orphaned from this staker's point of view.
suggested-fix: Call `_syncBudget()` at the start of `setDispatcherHook` so any pending mint-debt on the OLD dispatcher is pulled in before the pointer is updated. Also add a zero-address check (or at least document that zero-address disables pulls). Consider emitting an additional event or warning when the swap leaves a non-zero mint-debt behind.
